test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements is/are true about Non-Functional Dimensions (NF) in engineering drawing?

Statement 1: Non-functional Dimensions are shown without limits, as they do not affect the functionality of the component or space.

Statement 2: Non-Functional Dimensions are typically used for reference purposes only, and do not impact the assembly or performance of the component or space.
solution:
The correct answer is __Only statement 2 is true.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Non-Functional Dimensions__ are dimensions that do not directly affect the functionality or performance of a component or space.
 
• Such dimensions are generally used for reference purposes, documentation, or ease of manufacturing and inspection.
 
• Statement 1 is incorrect as Non-Functional Dimensions may be shown with or without limits, depending on their purpose.
 
• Statement 2 is correct as Non-Functional Dimensions do not impact the assembly or functional performance of the component or space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Functional Dimensions:**

 
 
• These are critical dimensions that directly affect the functionality, assembly, or performance of a component.
 
• Functional dimensions are typically controlled with tight tolerances.
 
 
 
• **Reference Dimensions: **
 
 
• These are dimensions provided for informational purposes only.
 
• They do not have tolerances and are not inspected during quality control.
 
 
 
• **Auxiliary Dimensions:**
 
 
• These are additional dimensions used to support the main dimensions, often for clarity or inspection purposes.
 
• These may or may not have tolerances depending on their function.
